claims.text: AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a newer execution can overtake an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping the waiting execution before it starts.
If a CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` is busy and enough commits land, a queued CodePipeline execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue so each one runs in turn.
CodePipeline's `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (`pipelineType` V2).
The AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands accept `executionMode` and `pipelineType` settings in the pipeline definition.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider has `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The linked AWS CodePipeline user guide page 'concepts-how-it-works' documents CodePipeline execution modes including SUPERSEDED.
The Pulumi registry page /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ exists for the aws.codepipeline.Pipeline resource.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that a deployment job targets, which can prevent concurrent runs from reaching the same stack.
In Azure DevOps, the exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is a stage-level property that controls how the exclusive lock check applies to the stage referencing the environment.
The default value of `lockBehavior` in Azure Pipelines is `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage runs against the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud itself serializes updates to a stack, one at a time.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
The Pulumi Azure Pipelines task `Pulumi@1` accepts inputs `command`, `stack`, and `args`, with `command: up` and `args: --yes`.
The page links to a troubleshooting page on update conflicts at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/.
When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one run.
When two concurrent runs target the same stack, the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict error.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' located under the configuration's General Settings.
The default value of TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option is 0, meaning unlimited.
With TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' set to 1, a second build is queued behind the first and runs only once the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud's per-stack lease provides one-at-a-time update behavior for a stack.
The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists and describes update conflicts.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by a deployment job serializes Pulumi deployments.
In Azure Pipelines, `lockBehavior: sequential` is a valid setting on a stage, used together with an exclusive lock check on the environment so that runs queue sequentially.
The Pulumi docs have a page at /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ with a section anchored 'serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode is SUPERSEDED, in which a newer execution supersedes an older execution that is still waiting to start.
AWS CodePipeline pipelines have an 'execution mode' setting with a `QUEUED` value.
The Pulumi docs have a page at /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ with a section anchored 'serialize-pipeline-executions'.
In TeamCity, setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 on a build configuration serializes deployments.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds'.
The Pulumi docs have a TeamCity guide at /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ with a section anchored 'limit-concurrent-builds'.
